newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bamerindus' owner may give up control of the bank.
newsitem.headline: Bamerindus' owner may give up control of the bank.

text.p: Brazilian Senator Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira has hinted he may give up control of private bank Bamerindus under an agreement with the Central Bank to rescue the bank, Folha de Sao Paulo daily said.
In this case, Vieira, who had refused to consider giving up control of the bank, would become a minority shareholder, without making decisions regarding the bank's management, the newspaper said.
According to Folha, Vieira's willingness to consider selling a controlling stake in the bank should pave the way for the Central Bank to grant Bamerindus a special credit line in October.
In recent months, Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth-largest private bank, has been struggling to recover liquidity, restore public confidence and fight speculation that the bank would be sold.
Newspapers also have reported the bank has been in talks with other institutions for a possible merger.
